headline: Single-cell and spatial profiling resolves tumor-stroma-immune niches linked to outcome
label: Single Cell Tumor Microenvironment Profiling
summary: Spatial and single-cell transcriptomics now map tumor-immune-stromal niches in situ, relating them to immune exclusion, outcome, and therapy response.
synthesis: The common thread is single-cell and spatial transcriptomics used to resolve tumor microenvironment states in situ and relate them to immune context and clinical outcome. In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, one study identifies invasive-frontier myCAFs and a tumor-stroma community associated with worse TCGA-PAAD outcomes, and another links an SPP1-CD44 endothelial-macrophage axis to S100A6 upregulation. In lung adenocarcinoma, a JUNB+ neutrophil subset is enriched in immune-excluded regions, and CHCHD3 upregulation is linked to chemoimmunotherapy resistance. In hepatocellular carcinoma, a mature TLS-associated spatial niche is inversely associated with ACC1-related lipid metabolism. Glioblastoma and neuroblastoma studies resolve iron-associated invasive states and ADRN/MES states. Many other entries are bulk-driven signature analyses or reviews, so this thread does not apply uniformly. What is new is niche-level, spatially resolved characterization of these states rather than bulk signatures alone.
